message.content: All three open claims can be tested independently with bit-exact sweeps against an FP64/multiple-precision oracle, so I'll launch three probes together: c1 (full finite-FP16-domain sweep with mpmath tie verification), c2 (negative-tail subnormal/underflow region), and c3 (edge inputs and non-multiple-of-256 tail masking).

{"claim_id": "c1", "code": "import importlib.util, json, struct
import torch
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("kernel", "/root/cases/case_149/kernel.py")
kernel = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(kernel)

# All finite FP16 encodings
codes = [i for i in range(65536)]
vals = torch.tensor(codes, dtype=torch.uint16).view(torch.float16)
finite = torch.isfinite(vals)
xf = vals[finite]
print("num_finite_fp16_inputs", xf.numel())

# run in one call (65504 <= 131072)
xc = xf.to("cuda")
out = kernel.run(xc)

# reference: FP64 sigmoid -> RNE binary16 via struct '<e'
xd = xc.cpu().to(torch.float64)
ref = torch.tensor([struct.unpack("<e", struct.pack("<e", v))[0] for v in torch.sigmoid(xd).tolist()], dtype=torch.float16).to("cuda")

ob = out.view(torch.int16).cpu()
rb = ref.view(torch.int16).cpu()
mism = (ob != rb).nonzero().flatten()
print("mismatch_count", mism.numel())

# mpmath verification of true single-rounding for mismatches
import mpmath
mpmath.mp.dps = 60
def true_fp16(x):
    v = mpmath.sigmoid(mpmath.mpf(float(x)))
    packed = struct.pack("<e", float(v))
    return struct.unpack("<e", packed)[0]
details = []
for idx in mism.tolist()[:50]:
    xval = xc[idx].item()
    t = true_fp16(xval)
    details.append({"x": repr(xval), "kernel_bits": int(ob[idx].item()) & 0xFFFF,
                    "ref_bits": int(rb[idx].item()) & 0xFFFF,
                    "mpmath_bits": struct.unpack("<H", struct.pack("<e", t))[0]})
real_fail = sum(1 for d in details if d["kernel_bits"] != d["mpmath_bits"])
print(json.dumps({"claim": "c1", "metric": "exact FP16 bit equality vs mpmath single-rounding",
  "n_inputs": xf.numel(), "mismatch_vs_fp64ref": int(mism.numel()),
  "mpmath_verified_kernel_wrong": real_fail, "details": details}))
", "expected_signal": "any bit mismatch where kernel FP32 path rounds differently than true single-rounding (mpmath-verified)"}

{"claim_id": "c2", "code": "import importlib.util, json, struct
import torch
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("kernel", "/root/cases/case_149/kernel.py")
kernel = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(kernel)

# all finite negative FP16 inputs with x <= -16 (covers subnormal/zero output region and beyond)
codes = torch.arange(65536, dtype=torch.uint16)
vals = codes.view(torch.float16)
sel = torch.isfinite(vals) & (vals <= -16.0) & (vals < 0)
x = vals[sel]
print("n_neg_tail_inputs", x.numel())
xc = x.to("cuda")
out = kernel.run(xc)

xd = xc.cpu().to(torch.float64)
ref = torch.tensor([struct.unpack("<e", struct.pack("<e", v))[0] for v in torch.sigmoid(xd).tolist()], dtype=torch.float16).to("cuda")
ob = out.view(torch.int16).cpu(); rb = ref.view(torch.int16).cpu()
mism = (ob != rb).nonzero().flatten()
# classify outputs: subnormals, zeros, negative zeros
def is_sub(h): return (int(h) & 0x7C00) == 0 and (int(h) & 0x03FF) != 0
sub_out = sum(1 for h in ob.tolist() if is_sub(h)); sub_ref = sum(1 for h in rb.tolist() if is_sub(h))
neg_zero_out = sum(1 for h in ob.tolist() if (int(h) & 0xFFFF) == 0x8000)
pos_zero_out = sum(1 for h in ob.tolist() if int(h) == 0)
mism_details = [{"x": repr(xc[i].item()), "kernel_bits": hex(int(ob[i]) & 0xFFFF), "ref_bits": hex(int(rb[i]) & 0xFFFF)} for i in mism.tolist()[:30]]
print(json.dumps({"claim": "c2", "metric": "exact FP16 bit equality, subnormal preservation, zero sign",
  "n_inputs": int(x.numel()), "mismatches": int(mism.numel()),
  "subnormal_out_kernel": sub_out, "subnormal_out_ref": sub_ref,
  "neg_zero_out": neg_zero_out, "pos_zero_out": pos_zero_out,
  "details": mism_details}))
", "expected_signal": "subnormal outputs flushed to zero, negative zero, or bit mismatches in the negative tail"}

{"claim_id": "c3", "code": "import importlib.util, json, struct
import torch
spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("kernel", "/root/cases/case_149/kernel.py")
kernel = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec); spec.loader.exec_module(kernel)

edge = [0.0, -0.0, 65504.0, -65504.0, 16.0, 17.0, 17.5, 18.0, 18.5, 19.0, 20.0, 24.0,
        6.1e-5, -6.1e-5, 5.96e-8, -5.96e-8, 1.0, -1.0, 11.09, -11.09]
xe = torch.tensor(edge, dtype=torch.float16).to("cuda")
oute = kernel.run(xe)
refe = kernel.reference(xe)
ok_edge = bool((oute.view(torch.int16) == refe.view(torch.int16)).all())
edge_bits = [{"x": repr(v), "k": hex(int(b) & 0xFFFF), "r": hex(int(rb) & 0xFFFF)}
             for v, b, rb in zip(edge, oute.view(torch.int16).cpu().tolist(), refe.view(torch.int16).cpu().tolist())]

# masked-tail: N=4093 random full-domain
g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(7)
xr = (30.0 * (torch.rand(4093, generator=g) * 2 - 1)).to(torch.float16).to("cuda")
outr = kernel.run(xr); refr = kernel.reference(xr)
tail_ok = bool((outr.view(torch.int16) == refr.view(torch.int16)).all())
tail_mism = int((outr.view(torch.int16) != refr.view(torch.int16)).sum())

# also last-lane check: a tensor where only the final element is nonzero signal
xq = torch.zeros(4093, dtype=torch.float16); xq[-1] = 65504.0
xq = xq.to("cuda")
oq = kernel.run(xq); fq = kernel.reference(xq)
last_ok = bool((oq.view(torch.int16) == fq.view(torch.int16)).all())
print(json.dumps({"claim": "c3", "metric": "exact FP16 bit equality on edge inputs and non-multiple-of-256 N",
  "edge_inputs_ok": ok_edge, "tail_n4093_ok": tail_ok, "tail_mismatch_count": tail_mism,
  "last_lane_ok": last_ok, "edge_bits": edge_bits}))
", "expected_signal": "edge or tail-mask mismatches vs bit-exact reference"}

message.reasoning_content:
Design probes: c1 — sweep all finite FP16 inputs? 65536 values, run kernel vs reference (mpmath or FP64 plus check near ties). But N ≤ 131072, so we can run full sweep of all 65536 finite codes in chunks. Reference = kernel's own reference() function, but that's FP64 sigmoid — the contract's true value. For c1 we also want high-precision check: use mpmath for near-tie cases. Simpler: run full sweep of all finite FP16 inputs through run() (in chunks of 131072 — 65536 fits), compare bit-exact against reference(). That covers c1, c2, c3 largely. But claims are separate; I can run one probe per claim with targeted subsets.

c1 probe: full sweep, compare with FP64-rounded reference AND for mismatches compute mpmath 50-digit sigmoid to confirm true rounding. 
c2 probe: x in negative range producing subnormals/zeros.
c3 probe: zeros, ±65504, near-1 cliff values, N=4093 tail check.

Actually a single full sweep covers everything; but run_claim_probe targets one claim each. I'll do three probes: c1 full sweep with mpmat verification; c2 negative-tail subset; c3 edges + N=4093. All independent — launch all three together.

Note kernel run must use CUDA; available (T4). Write code: import kernel module from artifact path. Path: /root/cases/case_149/kernel.py. Use importlib.

c1 code: build all finite fp16 bit patterns (65536), filter non-NaN/inf; run in chunks (validate requires N≤131072, 65536 fine). Compare bits to reference computed via FP64 sigmoid + struct '<e' — reference function requires tensor ≤131072; ok. For mismatches, mpmath check. Print JSON.

c2: generate all negative finite fp16 inputs whose sigmoid is subnormal/zero (x roughly ≤ -17.5?). Compute set, run, compare with reference, check sign of zero bits, subnormal bit patterns preserved.

c3: build edge array [0.0, -0.0, 65504, -65504, and values around 16.5-19 positive, smallest subnormal inputs etc.], N=4093 with values including last lane arbitrary; compare all.

Launch all three probes in one response.
